final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is useful in one respect: it correctly concedes that the case is not clean compliance and that operational-readiness evidence does not override the specific release-policy rule. But that concession is not enough to move the result to compliant_with_caveats. A caveated verdict would fit only if the remaining issue were a disclosure or communication caveat attached to an otherwise satisfied compliance predicate. Here, the unresolved item is itself the compliance predicate: whether certification without material weakness disclosure is permitted. On the present admissible record, the policy text points toward materiality because the below-target segment is named in customer commitments and legal review is pending. With no legal clearance, no approval for risk acceptance, and no underlying document showing nondisclosure is allowed, certifying now without disclosure remains noncompliant.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows a final legal determination that nondisclosure is permitted.

The policy text makes a weakness material when it affects a named launch use case or contractual customer segment, and the affected legal intake triage segment is described as named in two law-firm pilot commitments.
Legal review remains open, so the disclosure predicate is unresolved rather than satisfied.
Aggregate readiness and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness only; they do not satisfy the specific disclosure/materiality requirement.
No admissible evidence shows approved risk acceptance or release-governance authorization to certify despite the unresolved disclosure question.
